candidates.name: Trump reframes US-China relationship as peer powers
candidates.brief: China imposed export bans on United States rare earth companies, the Taipei Times reports. Trump convened Pentagon officials and defense companies to discuss ramping up missile production, TASS reports citing the Wall Street Journal.

captions.ig: The Supreme Court ruled on Trump's ability to fire Federal Reserve officials - and the same ruling produced nearly opposite headlines. One reading says the court blocked Trump and protected Fed independence. Another says the ruling expanded executive power, with the Fed as a narrow exception. What does the ruling actually establish? Both sides at adamkropacek.github.io/horus
captions.fb: The Supreme Court handed down a ruling on whether the president can remove Federal Reserve officials - and the coverage split sharply. Devdiscourse, Al Jazeera and South China Morning Post report the court blocked Trump's attempt to fire Fed governor Lisa Cook, framing the result as a defense of central bank independence. The Guardian and AP center a different aspect of the same ruling, describing it as an expansion of presidential removal power across the executive branch, with a narrow carve-out protecting the Fed specifically. Same text, opposite emphasis. Whether the ruling's core effect was a constraint or an expansion of executive authority depends on which element reporters chose as the story. Both sides at adamkropacek.github.io/horus
captions.li: The Supreme Court's ruling on presidential removal power generated divergent coverage that illustrates how the same legal decision can produce near-opposite narratives. Devdiscourse, Al Jazeera and South China Morning Post frame the ruling as a check on Trump - reporting that the court blocked his attempt to remove Fed governor Lisa Cook and reaffirmed the principle of central bank independence. The Guardian and AP lead with a different element: the ruling expanded presidential authority to fire officials across executive agencies, with a specific carve-out for the Fed rather than a general endorsement of institutional independence. The distinction carries real weight. If the first reading is operative, Fed independence was affirmed as a constitutional principle. If the second holds, it was preserved as an exception within a broader grant of executive authority - a meaningfully different baseline. Both sides at adamkropacek.github.io/horus
captions.x: Supreme Court ruling on firing the Fed governor - two outlets say Trump was blocked, two others say his removal power expanded. Both sides: adamkropacek.github.io/horus

split.a: Devdiscourse, Al Jazeera and South China Morning Post say the Supreme Court blocked Trump’s attempt to fire Fed governor Lisa Cook, upholding Fed independence.
split.b: Guardian World and © Julia Demaree Nikhinson, AP say the Supreme Court expanded Trump’s power to fire officials while protecting the Fed.
split.q: Did the Supreme Court limit or expand Trump's power to fire officials?
